px-[24px] py-[60px]"><header class="mb-[40px]"><h1 class="text-[36px] font-[600] leading-[1.3] text-brand-1 mb-[16px]">Introducing MiniMax Code Mini App</h1><div class="flex items-center gap-[16px] text-[14px] text-[#86909C]"><time>2026-10-22</time></div><div class="flex gap-[8px] mt-[16px] flex-wrap"><span class="px-[10px] py-[4px] text-[12px] bg-[#F4F4F4] text-zinc-700 rounded-[6px]">MiniMax Code</span><span class="px-[10px] py-[4px] text-[12px] bg-[#F4F4F4] text-zinc-700 rounded-[6px]">Mini App</span><span class="px-[10px] py-[4px] text-[12px] bg-[#F4F4F4] text-zinc-700 rounded-[6px]">Agent</span></div></header><div class="prose max-w-none text-[16px] leading-[1.8] text-brand-1"><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">A Mini App is a long-running application with a frontend and a backend. It installs as a plugin, calls and is called by the Agent, and keeps the Agent’s work on a page that stays live.</p><div class="html-block"><img src="https://file.cdn.minimax.io/public/minimax-code-mini-app-overseas-cover-1-1792651248999.jpg?x-oss-process=image/format,webp" alt="Cover: a hand places a card into a cluster of Mini Apps, including a stock dashboard, a 3D model, a map, and a chat, connected by a line to the Agent" width="2400" height="1350" style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;margin:12px 0;border-radius:12px" /></div><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">Today, we’re launching <a href="https://agent.minimax.io/docs/miniapp/overview" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">Mini App</a> in the MiniMax Code desktop app. A Mini App is a long-running application with a frontend and a backend. It installs as a plugin, and it and the Agent can call each other. Our goal is to keep the Agent’s work on a page that stays live, instead of scattered across conversations.</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">A lot of work is already handed to Agents, from refactoring code to sorting through messages. But each task moves forward in its own conversation. Before picking one back up, you have to dig through a pile of conversations for the context and remember what that one was for. Asking the Agent for an HTML dashboard pulls the information into one place, but the page only shows the data from the moment it was generated. To keep it updated, push a task forward, or save results, you have to go back to the chat and explain everything again. Work between people and AI is never handed off just once: sometimes it needs a human’s revisions, and sometimes it needs the AI to pitch in.</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">Agent plugins let you change the Agent. Mini Apps let you build applications on top of it. System-level concerns like ports, the Agent, and the data directory belong to the host, MiniMax Code, which draws the boundaries between them. What the tool looks like is up to you: just tell the Agent.</p><h2 class="text-2xl font-bold mb-4 mt-6">Mini Apps</h2><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">A Mini App is an extension compatible with the <a href="https://agent.minimax.io/docs/code/agents/plugin-submission" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">MiniMax Plugin protocol</a>, with a <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-sm">miniapp.json</code> manifest, a frontend, and a Node.js server added on top. The architecture is straightforward: the Node.js server fetches data, saves results, and exposes the app’s features to the Agent through hosted MCP. The page appears in the conversation sidebar and can pop out into its own window. Processes, ports, authentication, credentials, and rollback-capable publishing are all handled by the host.</p><div class="html-block"><img src="https://file.cdn.minimax.io/public/minimax-code-mini-app-overseas-architecture-2-1792651248999.jpg?x-oss-process=image/format,webp" alt="Mini App architecture: Mini Apps installed as plugins, each with its own page, Node server, and data, sit above the host, MiniMax Code, which provides the port, the Agent, and the data directory. The two call each other through hosted MCP and the Agent API, and you tell the Agent what tool you want" width="2400" height="1500" style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;margin:12px 0;border-radius:12px" /></div><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">Today’s release has three parts:</p><ul class="list-disc pl-6 mb-4 space-y-1"><li class="leading-relaxed">The Mini App runtime: a Node backend with a persistent data directory, hosted MCP, the Agent API, Host Connectors, and tool approvals handled right in the page</li><li class="leading-relaxed"><code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-sm">/miniapp-creator</code>: go from a one-sentence request in chat to a working page</li><li class="leading-relaxed">Official Mini Apps in the plugin marketplace, plus MiniMax-Code-MiniApps, the open-source community repository</li></ul><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">With <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-sm">/miniapp-creator</code>, the Agent first runs a read-only query against each data source to confirm it can get real data. Then it writes the page and the backend, publishes the app, opens it, and checks the result with screenshots in the built-in browser.</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">Several of the first official Mini Apps were built this way by colleagues outside our engineering team:</p><ul class="list-disc pl-6 mb-4 space-y-1"><li class="leading-relaxed">A stock dashboard Mini App brings stock information scattered across Knowledge Planet (Zsxq), Jinmen Finance, and Tencent Docs into a single dashboard.</li><li class="leading-relaxed">CadQuery Viewer lets you mark positions on a 3D model and send them back to the conversation for the Agent to change.</li><li class="leading-relaxed">Self-drive Route Planner combines map routing, place search, and image generation into one trip-planning workspace.</li><li class="leading-relaxed">MiniMax Bot is itself a Mini App. The main bot assembles a team, hands long-running tasks to background Agent conversations, then reviews and reports on the results. Agents in those conversations can in turn call the Bot’s tools to send messages and to save and search memories. Most Bot updates only require a plugin change, with no need to wait for a MiniMax Code release. Its source code is now in the open-source community repository.</li></ul><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">Developers in the open-source community have started building their own Mini Apps, too: a dashboard of token usage by date and model, Git Commit Tree for browsing Git history as a swimlane graph, and Session Trajectory for replaying a conversation’s model trajectory. Some lean toward everyday life and creative work, like Xinyu Island, for logging your mood and drawing a daily inspiration card, and Anatomy Gallery, where the Agent creates and edits interactive diagrams.</p><blockquote class="border-l-4 border-gray-300 pl-4 my-4 italic text-gray-700"><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">“From early workflows to RAG and Agentic Search, and inspired by our work at MiniMax, I’ve found that professional work needs something more than a flashy Agent: a native, tightly integrated environment where Agents and people work closely together. As a financial analyst, I used to spend most of my time pulling together scattered information. Now that Mini Apps bring it into my workspace, I can focus on thinking and judgment, and leave organizing, analyzing, and working through the information entirely to the Mini Apps.”</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">— Product Manager at MiniMax</p></blockquote><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">On security: account credentials are held by the host, and neither plugins nor pages can access them. Connectors and Agent permissions must be declared in the manifest before they can be used. A Mini App’s server port is open only to its own pages and the Agent. When a page wants to pass something to the Agent, the content goes into your input box first, so you can review and edit it before sending. <strong>Mini App code runs on your machine as you, so only install packages from sources you trust.</strong></p><h2 class="text-2xl font-bold mb-4 mt-6">Getting started</h2><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">Mini Apps are available now in local sessions of the MiniMax Code desktop app (macOS / Windows).</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">You can install ready-made Mini Apps from the plugin marketplace, or describe what you need in chat and have the Agent build one on the spot. After using it for a while, ask the Agent to adjust it to the way you work.</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">To start building:</p><ul class="list-disc pl-6 mb-4 space-y-1"><li class="leading-relaxed">Download MiniMax Code: <a href="https://agent.minimax.io/download" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">https://agent.minimax.io/download</a> (mainland China: <a href="https://agent.minimax.cn/download" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">https://agent.minimax.cn/download</a>)</li><li class="leading-relaxed">Follow the quickstart to build your first Mini App with <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-sm">/miniapp-creator</code>: <a href="https://agent.minimax.io/docs/miniapp/authors/quickstart" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">https://agent.minimax.io/docs/miniapp/authors/quickstart</a></li></ul><h2 class="text-2xl font-bold mb-4 mt-6">An open community</h2><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">The source code for MiniMax Bot and the community’s Mini Apps all live in the open-source repository <a href="https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Code-MiniApps" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">MiniMax-Code-MiniApps</a>. If you’ve built a Mini App you find useful, we’d love for you to share it with a pull request.</p><p class="mb-4 leading-relaxed">If you need a runtime capability Mini Apps don’t have yet, leave a comment on the pinned <a href="https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Code-MiniApps/issues/9" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="text-blue-600 underline hover:text-blue-800">capability wishlist</a> in the community repository.</p></div></article><footer class="bg-black px-6 md:px-[60px] pt-20 pb-10"><div class="max-w-[1920px] mx-auto"></div></footer></body></html>
